result.note: Official monthly trade data; tests the direction of exports, the trade deficit and gold imports rather than precise decimals.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's merchandise trade data for August 2026, released in September 2026:
items: Goods exports rose by more than a quarter year-on-year to about USD 43.8 billion.
The trade deficit narrowed compared with August 2025.
Gold imports fell by more than half year-on-year.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: All three are correct. Exports grew 26.1% to USD 43.81 billion and the trade deficit narrowed against a year earlier, while gold imports fell 57.75%. Despite the strong export growth, the deficit narrowed by just USD 360 million, and the fall in gold imports did most of the work.
questions.source: India's goods exports rose 26.1% year-on-year in August to USD 43.81 billion, yet the trade deficit narrowed just USD 360 million against a year earlier, as a 57.75% fall in gold imports did the heavy lifting.
